goal: decision-models S1 (from #204; BR-DEC-7; delivers #284 S1 item 7, docs/specs/review-verifier-eval.spec.md:307-317). A maintainer can see, per run and acceptance ID, how review findings repeated across rounds, from committed records only. acceptance.assertion: In tests/acceptance-repeat-series.test.ts, acceptanceRepeatSeries returns: for key A with findings in rounds 1, 2 and 3 and latestRound 3, finding_count 3, rounds_with_findings 3, last_finding_round 3, rounds_since_last_finding 0, current_streak 3; for key B with one finding in round 1 and latestRound 3, rounds_since_last_finding 2 and current_streak 0; two findings of one key in the same round give finding_count 2 and rounds_with_findings 1; a finding with acceptance_id null is reported under the null key; a finding with review_round null raises finding_count and unrounded but no round metric; an empty findings list returns an empty series.

In tests/acceptance-repeat-series.test.ts, scripts/review-eval/acceptance-repeats.ts run as a subprocess with --root on a temporary git repository whose HEAD commits one run-scoped audit pair with findings on two acceptance IDs prints, with --json, one row per (run, acceptance) whose counts equal acceptanceRepeatSeries over that run; an audit pair present only in the working tree and not committed is absent from the output; git status --porcelain of the temporary repository is unchanged after the run; a --root that is not a git repository exits 1 with the error on stderr and no stdout rows.
docs/specs/review-verifier-eval.spec.md item 7 (Per-acceptance repeat counts) states that the series is delivered by the decision-models S1 task acceptance-repeat-series and that #284 S1 reuses it.
